citation.title: Artificial neural network supported design of a lattice-based artificial spinal disc for restoring patient-specific anisotropic behaviors
citation.authors: Zhiyang Yu; Prakash Thakolkaran; Kristina Shea; Tino Stanković
citation.version_coded: open-access version of record, author-uploaded full text

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: The surrogate-assisted disc optimization is said to finish in about 40 seconds, versus an estimated 24 hours for optimization using finite-element analysis at every evaluation.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: [inferred] §5.2 gives about 24 h for FE-based optimization and about 40 s for ANN-assisted optimization; 24 × 3600 / 40 = 2160. The FE-based duration is prospective wording, not a documented completed run.
claim.alternatives: Abstract and §6 qualitatively claim faster or more efficient optimization; §4 compares stiffness predictions from MLP and CNN against FE results.

baseline.classical_method: Genetic algorithm with FE structural analysis for fitness evaluation (§3.3, §5.2)
baseline.implementation: MATLAB 1D beam-element structural analysis (§3.1.4); FE-in-the-loop GA implementation not stated
baseline.hardware_classical: Intel Core i7-8550U CPU, 16 GB RAM for all computational tasks (§3, workflow)
baseline.hardware_ml: Intel Core i7-8550U CPU, 16 GB RAM for all computational tasks (§3, workflow)
baseline.problem_size: 15 × 3 × 2 lattice grid, 90 unit-cell assignment variables (§3.3, Table 2)
baseline.classical_iterations: 500 GA generations and population size 50 specified for ANN-assisted optimization (§3.3, Table 2); FE-based comparator iteration count not separately stated
baseline.classical_time: around 24 h, estimated for FE-analysis-based optimization (§5.2)
baseline.training_time: 500 training epochs, wall time not stated (§3.2)
baseline.data_generation_cost: 600,000 FE-analysed samples per unit-cell library, two libraries; wall time not stated (§3.1.4)
baseline.quality_metric: Six rotational stiffnesses compared with target disc; final design FE-validated (§3.3, Figs. 9 and 13)
baseline.quality_gap: No optimized result from FE-in-the-loop GA is reported for quality comparison (§5.2)

R1.evidence: §5.2 compares optimization durations without a quality result for the FE-based GA comparator; Figs. 9 and 13 validate only the returned ANN-assisted designs.

R2.evidence: §3 and §5.2 place tasks on one CPU machine, but give no FE-baseline solver, actual iteration timing, or convergence plot establishing R2(a)–(e).

R3.evidence: §3.1.4 reports 600,000 FE-labelled samples per library and §3.2 gives 500 training epochs, but §5.2's 40 s claim omits their wall times and gives no break-even use count.

R4.evidence: §3.3 and Figs. 9/13: optimized discs are checked by FE analysis, but no failure or infeasibility rate across optimization runs is given.

reporting.n_test_cases: 2 target lumbar disc levels, L2–L3 and L4–L5, studied with two unit-cell libraries (§4.2–4.3)

notes: The 24 h FE-based optimizer time is phrased prospectively in §5.2; no completed classical optimization run or classical design quality is documented. The author-uploaded version of record was readable through ResearchGate; the ETH repository download returned HTTP 429.
